title: Build a 4-bit serial-in shift register
statement_md: Create a module named `shift_reg4` with `clk`, a synchronous active-high `reset`, a serial input `serial_in` and a 4-bit output `q`. On every rising edge, if `reset` is 1 then `q` becomes 0000. Otherwise `q` shifts towards the MSB: `q[3]` takes `q[2]`, `q[2]` takes `q[1]`, `q[1]` takes `q[0]` and `q[0]` takes `serial_in`.

tests.hint: reset=1 at a rising edge must clear q to 0000.
The new bit enters at q[0]; check the intended next state is {q[2:0], serial_in}.

tests.purpose: builds a pattern over several edges
tests.hint: Shift several bits in a row and confirm the running pattern matches, not just the first shift.
Shifting a 0 in should push existing bits toward the MSB and drop the oldest bit.

tests.purpose: drops the oldest bit out of q[3]
tests.hint: After enough shifts no original bit should remain. Check that the earliest bit really leaves at q[3].

tests.purpose: waits for the edge to apply reset
tests.hint: Toggling reset between clock edges must not change q until the next rising edge.

hints: The next value of q is the old q shifted left by one, with serial_in in the lowest bit.
A concatenation such as {q[2:0], serial_in} describes the whole shift in one line.
Use non-blocking assignments so every bit moves on the same edge.
